questions.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: $\frac{1}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 - \sin x}$.
questions.answer: Combine fractions: $\frac{(1 - \sin x) + (1 + \sin x)}{(1 + \sin x)(1 - \sin x)} = \frac{2}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x$.

questions.q: Which of the following is equal to $\tan x + \cot x$?
questions.answer: $\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x} = \sec x \csc x$.

questions.q: Find all solutions to $2\cos^2 x + \cos x - 1 = 0$ in $[0, 2\pi)$.
questions.answer: Factor: $(2\cos x - 1)(\cos x + 1) = 0$. $\cos x = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}$. $\cos x = -1 \Rightarrow x = \pi$.

questions.q: How many solutions does $\sin(3x) = \frac{1}{2}$ have in the interval $[0, 2\pi)$?
questions.answer: As $x$ ranges over $[0, 2\pi)$, $3x$ covers three complete cycles $[0, 6\pi)$. Since $\sin u = 1/2$ has $2$ solutions per cycle, there are $3 \times 2 = 6$ solutions.
$\tan x = \pm \sqrt{3}$. On $[0, \pi]$, $\tan x = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\tan x = -\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow x = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Laws of Sines & Cosines with Ambiguous Case

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $a = 12, b = 15,$ and angle $A = 30^\circ$. How many valid triangles can be formed?
questions.answer: Calculate altitude $h = b \sin A = 15 \sin 30^\circ = 7.5$. Since $h < a < b$ ($7.5 < 12 < 15$), this is the ambiguous case yielding $2$ distinct triangles.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $a = 5, b = 7,$ and $c = 8$. What is the measure of angle $C$?
What is the area of a parallelogram with side lengths $8$ cm and $12$ cm and an acute interior angle of $45^\circ$?
What is the phase shift of the sinusoidal wave $y = 3\sin(2x - \frac{\pi}{3}) + 4$?
questions.answer: Factor out frequency: $2(x - \frac{\pi}{6})$. The phase shift is $\frac{\pi}{6}$ units to the right.

questions.q: What are the minimum and maximum values of the function $f(t) = 5 - 4\cos(3t)$?
questions.answer: Since $-1 \leq \cos(3t) \leq 1$, $-4 \leq -4\cos(3t) \leq 4$. Adding $5$ gives minimum $5 - 4 = 1$ and maximum $5 + 4 = 9$.

questions.q: What is the frequency (cycles per unit of $x$) of the function $y = \cos(4\pi x)$?
questions.answer: Period $T = \frac{2\pi}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2}$. Frequency is the reciprocal of the period: $f = \frac{1}{T} = 2$ cycles per unit.
